"Sync Redis inside the response output filter. DevExpressProxyResponseFilter.Close() and HtmlRewriteFilter.Close() both call ConfigurationInfo.GetGlobalConfigurationValue("UrlSlug", platformID) → blocking RedisDatabase.StringGet. "Izenda pumps a WinForms message loop inside w3wp. AsyncDataSetFiller.FillDataSet waits on its async DB fill via System.Windows.Forms.Application.ThreadContext.RunMessageLoop. Highest-scoring prod finding."

Investigation summary. LPUser queries on the Tailored Brands database averaged 0.5 to 0.8 seconds through August 5 and jumped to an average of 57 seconds with a 120-second maximum starting August 6, with the first bad plan appearing at 17:35 UTC. Same query IDs, new execution plans. The good ones were compiled with cardinality estimator 140, while the bad ones were compiled with 160.
All 137 production databases are now on compatibility level 160. Three are affected out of the 39 currently running this query.
The 120-second ceiling is the application CommandTimeout, and Cloudflare cuts at 100 seconds, which produces the 524.
Shared with Matt K, pending Engineering direction.

A user who is already in your daily SSO files with the correct permissions does not need to attempt a login and then wait. Where that has been happening it was not normal timing, it was an issue on our side, and it is now fixed.
It may help to clear up the sequence, because I did not draw it well enough before. There is no step where a user logs in and then waits up to 24 hours for that attempt to take effect. fields.description:
Customer 209 TBI supplies several SSO mapping files that are loaded to ARDM and then replicated to the Secure platform to manage user access. With platform unification, which TBI is actively using, we need to expand sso mapping to support incident level security assignments.

Requirements:

  1. Create new ARDM table to hold data (ie. ardm_209.sso_securitylevelassignments). The table should have these columns:

    1. username (varchar(256)) not null

    2. securityid (int) not null

    3. inserteddatetime (timetamp) not null

  2. Be sure to add create table script to the repo and give secure db account permission to access table.

  3. The customer is passing security levels in the currently supplied teams file which is loaded to tlog_209.appriss_sso_teams. Therefore data will be derived from tlog_209.appriss_sso_teams as follows:

    TRUNCATE TABLE ardm_209.sso_securitylevelassignments;
WITH latest_file as (select max(filename) as latest_filename from tlog_209.appriss_sso_teams)
INSERT INTO ardm_209.sso_securitylevelassignments
SELECT
 t.username as username
,case when t.team = 'Administrators' then 13
      when t.team = 'Risk Management' then 14
	  when t.team = 'Corporate User' then 11
	  when t.team = 'Field Loss Prevention' then 2
	  when t.team = 'Division Manager' then 6
	  when t.team = 'Regional Manager' then 7
	  when t.team = 'District Manager' then 8
	  when t.team = 'Location Manager' then 5
	  when t.team = 'Recruiter Fraud User' then 19
 else 0 end as securityid
,now() as inserteddatetime
FROM tlog_209.appriss_sso_teams as t
join latest_file on latest_file.latest_filename = t.filename
WHERE t.team in (
	'Field Loss Prevention',
	'Location Manager',
	'Division Manager',
	'Regional Manager',
	'District Manager',
	'Corporate User',
	'Administrators',
	'Risk Management',
	'Recruiter Fraud User'
	);

  4. Add ardm_209.sso_securitylevelassignments to replication. https://dev.azure.com/apprissdevops/Sysrepublic%20Secure/_git/arpfiles?path=/repo/209/system/yadl/Mappings.json

    1. source = sso_securitylevelassignments

    2. target = sso.securitylevelassignments

Investigation so far has confirmed the pipeline and file delivery are healthy, but a client-wide check now suggests the data itself may genuinely be stuck, not just reflecting normal per-user update behavior.

What we've confirmed is healthy:

  • Hatr task ReferenceDataBackLoad (client 209) has run successfully every day with zero failures (verified via Scheduled Task Logs dashboard, 7/7 successful runs, no errors).

  • Its BuildLocationHierarchy sub-task completes cleanly every run, same pattern.

This conflicts with TBI actively sending dedicated SSO-specific files daily. Not yet confirmed whether those files are actually being consumed anywhere in the codebase.

External input received:

  • Vlad (file monitoring) confirmed pipeline timing and suggested a timezone-display explanation - plausible for the baseline ~1 day lag the client considers normal, but doesn't explain two different sample users landing on two different, non-matching dates.

  • Carl Costelow (owns SSO implementations) confirmed the job runs daily per Hatr, suggested Support monitor for a week, and shared a saved Explorer report (SSO Max Inserted Date Time) for ongoing tracking.

This leans toward the data genuinely being stuck rather than the"updates only when something changes" theory we were working with earlier.

Root Cause Analysis — RCS-29027
Customer: Tailored Brands (client 209, TBI)

Summary: Location Name is blank on 100% of Secure Incident cases for Tailored Brands (220+ cases in the customer's Composer report, all stores, confirmed by customer to have never populated). Root cause confirmed via direct database query.

Root cause: incident.Location in Tailored Brands' production LPMS database (sqldb-prd-wus2-arp-production-209-tbi-platform) contains zero rows. Confirmed via SELECT * FROM incident.Location executed directly against that database — query ran successfully and returned the full expected column set (LocationID, ShopliftingID, LocationType, LocationName, Address1, Address2, City, State, Zip, Website, Notes, CreatedBy, CreatedDateTime), but with no rows at all. This table is populated per-case (via ShopliftingID), so an empty table means no case for this client has ever had a location record created.

How this surfaced: Customer added a "Location Name" column to a Composer/Explorer report and saw it blank across all 220+ results. The underlying Izenda SQL confirmed the field is sourced from a LEFT JOIN [incident].[Location] AS T4 ON (T2.ShopliftingID = T4.ShopliftingID) — i.e., a per-incident field, not the store master (incident.Store, which only supplies Division/StoreNo and is unrelated to this issue).

Cross-check performed: Before landing on this, we verified Tailored Brands' broader location reference pipeline is healthy — ardm_209.reference_location in Greenplum (fed by their LOC_LOCATION file via the ARDP ingestion process) has correct, complete retail store data, and Secure Store successfully resolves location names from it via StoreNo = LocationID. This confirms the underlying location data exists and is correct elsewhere in the platform; incident.Location in LPMS is a separate, LPMS-native table with no connection to that pipeline, and it's specifically this table that's empty.

Ask:

  1. Please confirm why incident.Location was never populated for this client — most likely a missed configuration/import step during Secure Incident onboarding.

  2. Confirm whether historical cases (220+ already on file) can be backfilled with location data, or whether this can only be fixed going forward for new cases.
@Megha Rathi The field the customer is looking for is Store.StoreName. Location table is a child table for an incident record. The store table holds various store attributes.

Confirmed fix. Rebuilt the report query joining StoreName from incident.Store (via T1.StoreIdent = T3.StoreIdent) instead of LocationName from incident.Location, and validated — store names return correctly. Per Ryan Barlow's guidance, incident.Location is a per-incident child table (unrelated to store identity) and was never the right source for this field. No data backfill needed — this was a report-definition issue, not a missing-data issue.

Hello Colton,

We found the issue. In Composer, the field you added (Location > Location Name) pulls from an incident-level record that isn't populated for your account. The field you actually want is Store > Store Name — that one does have your store data and should populate correctly.

To fix this on your end: in the Change Display Fields panel, remove Location Name, then search for and add Store Name instead. That should show the correct location for each case.

Let us know if you run into any issues adding it, or if you'd like us to update it for you.

Kind Regards,

Appriss Retail Support

This looks like a known, already-analysed Izenda reporting slowness problem in our own code, with performance fixes written but switched off for each client until enabled; it is not a Tailored Brands data problem. I can't confirm from here that those fixes are enabled for this client.

What we checked

  • The client notes for Tailored Brands have nothing on reporting slowness, and the cross-client incident list has no matching entry.

  • The client's configuration files have no reporting-related settings, so nothing there is client-specific to this report tool.

  • An existing engineering write-up covers the same symptoms: slow report pages, timeouts and "server side" errors after the move to shared hosting.

  • The performance fixes from that write-up are switched off by default per client, so they change nothing until someone turns them on for that client.

  • The write-up records an open mismatch where users see a timeout at roughly two minutes while the underlying query keeps running for up to ten minutes. That fits "times out, then blank page, retry".

  • A separate setting can send this report tool to its own dedicated server. That setting is off by default after an earlier outage.
